name: PasswordPal
summary: A zero-knowledge, local-first desktop password manager built with Tauri v2, React and Rust, where the vault is encrypted on the device before anything is synced.
whyItMatters: The server only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read. Keys are derived with Argon2id, vaults use AES-256-GCM, and a recovery key lets users reset a forgotten master password via an Ed25519 signature.

name: Distributed Auction System
summary: A fault-tolerant real-time online auction built in Go, where four independent nodes coordinate over RPC using classic distributed systems algorithms.
whyItMatters: It implements Bully election, Ricart-Agrawala mutual exclusion, two-phase commit with majority quorum, and Koo-Toueg checkpointing end-to-end, with crash recovery and transaction logging across laptops on Wi-Fi.

name: Talent Radar
summary: Ranks the top 100 of a 100,000-candidate pool for a Senior AI Engineer job description and writes a submission.csv with fact-checked reasoning for each finalist.
whyItMatters: Ranking runs CPU-only with no network or LLM calls in about 1 min 47 s, combining FAISS and BM25 retrieval with a Ridge ranker. Every explanation is audited against the candidate's own record, and the README documents its limitations.

name: Monday.com BI Agent
summary: A conversational Streamlit assistant that answers natural-language questions about sales pipeline and work order data pulled from two Monday.com boards.
whyItMatters: It normalizes messy data such as currency strings, mixed units and null values, and discloses anomalies in every answer. Tool figures are tested against independent pandas calculations from the raw Excel files.

name: SentinelFlow
summary: A multi-agent system built for a hackathon that turns meeting transcripts into tracked action items using LangChain, Vertex AI Gemini and AlloyDB, exposed through a FastAPI service.
whyItMatters: An Analyst agent extracts tasks with owners, deadlines and 768-dimension embeddings, and a Watchdog agent audits the database for unassigned tasks so action items are not silently dropped after a meeting.

name: PasswordPal Backend
summary: The Node.js and Express sync and account API for PasswordPal, backed by Supabase PostgreSQL, handling auth, 2FA, device management and encrypted vault sync.
whyItMatters: The server never receives the master password or any key that can decrypt a vault. It adds device-bound JWT sessions, Ed25519 signature-based recovery, shared brute-force rate limiting and delta sync with optimistic version locking.
